items.entity: Cantilever design domain (box dimensions, aspect ratio, absolute size)
items.description: Sec. 6.1.1 gives no dimensions. It only says the problem is 'the same as the numerical examples considered in [64]' and shows the domain in Fig. 3 (left), which is not available. The text gives only the design-variable counts (3,000/24,000/192,000; each mesh is 8x the previous, so each direction is halved per refinement) and a filter radius in physical units (r = 0.1 m). A box is assumed from 'structured mesh with uniform hexahedral elements'. Neither the aspect ratio nor the absolute size is determined, and the absolute size sets r relative to the domain.
readings: 3 m x 1 m x 1 m box (L:H:W = 3:1:1; cubic 0.1 m elements on a 30x10x10 coarse grid)
1 m x 1/3 m x 1/3 m box (3:1:1, unit length)
2 m x 1 m x 1 m box (2:1:1, non-cubic elements)
2 m x 1.5 m x 1 m box (4:3:2; 20x15x10 coarse grid)
6 m x 4 m x 1 m box (6:4:1; 30x20x5 coarse grid)

items.entity: Element grid (nelx x nely x nelz) for the 3,000 / 24,000 / 192,000-variable meshes
items.description: Sec. 6.1.1 gives only the total number of design variables and says 'a structured mesh with uniform hexahedral first-order finite elements' is used. It does not give the number of elements in each direction or say whether elements are cubic. One design variable per element is assumed from Sec. 2.

The text never says where the beam is supported. Only the word 'cantilever' and Fig. 3 (left, unavailable) imply that one end is fixed. Which face is fixed, and whether all of it or only part of it is constrained, is not given.
readings: Entire end face x = 0 (all nodes, 0<=y<=W, 0<=z<=H)
Only the nodes on the perimeter edges of the x = 0 face
Only the top and bottom edges of the x = 0 face
A central patch of the x = 0 face

items.entity: Constrained DOFs at the fixed end
items.description: 'Cantilever beam' (Sec. 6.1.1) implies a clamped end, but the text never says which displacement components are fixed.
readings: Clamped: ux = uy = uz = 0 on all support nodes
Only the axial (normal) displacement fixed on the face, plus minimal restraints to remove rigid-body motion

items.entity: Location of the applied load on the free end
items.description: The text never describes the load. Sec. 6.1.1 points to [64] and Fig. 3 (left, unavailable), so where the load sits on the free end (x = L) is unknown.
readings: Midpoint of the bottom edge of the free-end face (x = L, y = W/2, z = 0)
Centre of the free-end face (x = L, y = W/2, z = H/2)
Along the whole bottom edge of the free-end face (x = L, z = 0, 0<=y<=W)
Over the whole free-end face (x = L)
At a bottom corner of the free-end face (x = L, y = 0, z = 0), giving bending plus torsion

items.entity: Spatial distribution of the applied load
items.description: The text does not say whether the load is a single nodal force, a line load or a surface traction. The optimal compliance barely changes with mesh refinement (13.59 / 13.2 / 13.6 in Tables 1-3), which suggests a distributed load but does not prove it.
readings: Single nodal point force
Uniform line load along one edge of the free-end face (consistent nodal forces)
Uniform surface traction over the free-end face
Traction over a small patch (about 1-2 coarse elements wide) at the load location

items.description: The text gives no load direction; it appears only in Fig. 3, which is unavailable. If the cross-section is not square, choosing one transverse direction over the other changes the design.
readings: -z: transverse, along the beam height (vertical, downward)
-y: transverse, along the beam width

items.description: The cantilever has no load value anywhere in the text (Sec. 6.1.2 gives 10 N for the blade, but nothing is given for this example). The reported compliances (about 13.2-13.6, Tables 1-3) therefore cannot be matched in absolute terms.
readings: 1 N total force
1 N per loaded node
Unit traction (1 N/m^2) over the loaded edge or face
Magnitude chosen so the coarse-mesh compliance matches about 13.6 with the adopted E

items.description: Sec. 6.1.1 says 'The upper bound for the mass constraint is 0.5'. Eq. (1) defines v_u as an absolute bound on total material volume (sum of mu_i v_i), and a mass bound would need a density, which is not given. The text does not say whether 0.5 is a fraction of the domain volume or an absolute volume or mass.
readings: Volume fraction 0.5 (v_u = 0.5 x domain volume)
Absolute volume v_u = 0.5 m^3 (e.g. fraction 1/6 for a 3x1x1 m box)
Absolute mass 0.5 kg with an assumed density (the fraction then depends on density and domain size)

items.entity: Young's modulus E0 of the solid material
items.description: Printed as '2.0x10^{1}1 N/m^2' in Sec. 6.1.1 (the same typo appears in Sec. 6.1.2). It looks like a broken superscript, so the value can be read two ways.
readings: 2.0e11 N/m^2 (most likely intended; steel-like)
2.0e1 = 20 N/m^2 (literal rendering)

items.entity: Void (minimum) stiffness / lower density bound in SIMP
items.description: Eq. (4) E = rho^s E0, together with the bounds 0 <= mu <= 1 in Eq. (1), gives zero stiffness in void elements (a singular K). No minimum stiffness Emin or positive lower bound on mu or rho is stated for the example.
readings: Modified SIMP with Emin = 1e-9 E0
Modified SIMP with Emin = 1e-3 E0
Pure SIMP with a lower bound mu >= 1e-3

items.entity: Helmholtz filter radius r = 0.1 m relative to element size
items.description: Sec. 6.1.1 gives r in metres and appears to use it for all three meshes. Without domain dimensions the ratio r/h is unknown, so the effective length scale on each mesh is not determined.
readings: r/h = 2, 4, 8 (coarse h = 0.05 m)
r/h = 3, 6, 12 (unit-length 3:1:1 domain, coarse h = 1/30 m)
r/h = 0.5, 1, 2 (coarse h = 0.2 m)

items.entity: Helmholtz filter boundary conditions and discretisation
items.description: Eq. (3) is given without boundary conditions. The text also does not say how rho is discretised (nodal or element-wise) or mapped back to elements. A solver that has only a convolution filter would need a radius conversion, which the text does not give.
readings: Homogeneous Neumann BC on all boundaries; trilinear nodal rho on the same hex mesh, averaged to elements
Homogeneous Neumann BC; element-wise (cell-centred) discretisation
Padded/extended domain to suppress boundary effects
Equivalent convolution (cone) density filter with R = 2*sqrt(3)*r, about 0.35 m

items.description: The starting values of mu are not stated anywhere. The start point can matter: the paper reports that one run converged to a different local minimum (Table 1, incremental-SVD run).
readings: Uniform mu = 0.5 (equal to the volume bound)
Uniform mu = 1.0
Uniform mu slightly below the bound, e.g. 0.49 (strictly feasible)

items.description: The text gives only 'IPOPT ... convergence threshold of 10^-6'. It does not give the Hessian approximation, barrier-parameter strategy, scaling or iteration limit, and a standard topology-optimization solver would more likely use OC or MMA. Table 1 shows that different solution paths can reach different local minima.
readings: IPOPT, limited-memory BFGS Hessian, default adaptive barrier, tol = 1e-6
IPOPT, limited-memory BFGS Hessian, monotone barrier, tol = 1e-6
MMA with a KKT-residual stopping tolerance of 1e-6
OC update with a design-change stopping criterion

items.description: The text never mentions passive elements. Any non-design pads at the load or the support would appear only in Fig. 3 (left) or [64].
readings: None: the whole box is designable
Solid non-design pad under or around the load application region
Solid non-design layer at the clamped face

items.description: Eq. (2) writes the right-hand side as a design-dependent b(mu), and Eq. (8) includes db/dmu. Sec. 6.1.1 never says whether gravity acts, and no density is given.
readings: Design-independent external load only (db/dmu = 0)
External load plus self-weight proportional to rho (requires a density)

items.entity: Which cantilever configuration from [64] Fig. 3 represents
items.description: Sec. 6.1.1 says the problem is 'the same as the numerical examples considered in [64]' (plural) and that 'the design domains and optimal designs for two problems are shown in Figure 3'. The Fig. 3 caption, however, shows only one cantilever (left: domain, right: design). It is therefore unclear which setup from [64] is meant.
readings: A single cantilever configuration (Fig. 3 left) used for all three meshes
One of several cantilever variants in [64] (e.g. a different load placement or aspect ratio)
